rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic usage can substitute “the foolish person” for “foolishness”; by analogy, “those who are miserly” can stand for the omitted “miserliness.”
rows.anchor: فاكتفى عن السفه بالسفيه، كذلك اكتفى بالذين يبخلون من البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the second-person reading (ولا تحسبن); it supplies the subject of يحسبن, while “it is better for them” supplies its predicate, with miserliness understood.
rows.anchor: وأولى القراءتين بالصواب في ذلك عندي، قراءة من قرأ: (ولا تحسبن الذين يبخلون) بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person-plural? No: the third-person reading is not wrong, but it is less eloquent and less common in Arabic.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت القراءة بالياء غير خطأ، ولكنه ليس بالأفصح ولا الأشهر من كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns people who withhold from their worldly wealth the zakat God made obligatory, since they wrongly think that miserliness benefits them in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: فلا يخرجون منه حق الله الذي فرضه عليهم فيه من الزكوات

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies them as people given wealth who refused to spend it in God’s path and did not pay its zakat.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: (ولا تحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيرا لهم بل هو شر لهم) : «هم الذين آتاهم الله من فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the misers as Jews who concealed the Torah’s account and description of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى بذلك اليهود الذين بخلوا أن يبينوا للناس ما أنزل الله في التوراة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns the People of the Book, who withheld scripture instead of explaining it to people.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: (ولا تحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله) إلى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid likewise identifies the misers as Jews and connects the passage through the mention of the clear Book.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: (ولا تحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله) قال: «هم يهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the interpretation that they withheld zakat: Prophetic reports say the one who withholds God’s due will wear it as a serpent, and the next verse describes Jews calling God poor when ordered to give.
rows.anchor: وأولى التأويلين بتأويل هذه الآية التأويل الأول وهو أنه معنى بالبخل في هذا الموضع: منع الزكاة

rows.speaker: أبو مالك العبدي
rows.claim: Abu Malik says a person who refuses a needy relative from his surplus will have that withheld wealth brought forth as a bald serpent.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك العبدي، قال: «ما من عبد يأتيه ذو رحم له يسأله من فضل عنده فيبخل عليه إلا أخرج له

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says a refused relative’s claim to surplus wealth will become a Hell-serpent that licks its lips and collars the refuser.
rows.anchor: عن رجل، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما من ذي رحم يأتي رحمه فيسأله من فضل جعله الله عنده

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Qaz‘ah reports the Prophet’s warning that a refusing relative will face a fiery serpent that licks its lips and collars him; the Prophet recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي قزعة حجر بن بيان، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من ذي رحم يأتي ذا رحمه

rows.speaker: بهز بن حكيم
rows.claim: Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father and grandfather, reports that a man who refuses his dependent’s request for surplus wealth will face a serpent on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: عن بهز بن حكيم بن معاوية بن حيدة، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال: سمعت نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says the withheld wealth becomes a snake that pecks its owner’s head and says, “I am the wealth you withheld.”
rows.anchor: عن أبي وائل، عن عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud describes the withheld wealth as a serpent twisting around its owner’s head; another transmission calls it a black serpent.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا وائل، يحدث أنه سمع عبد الله، قال في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says the wealth will become a snake that pecks its owner’s head, identifies itself as his wealth, and coils around his neck.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي وائل، عن ابن مسعود، قال: " يجيء ماله يوم القيامة ثعبانا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says anyone who fails to pay zakat will be represented by a bald serpent that collars him; he recited the verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي وائل، عن ابن مسعود، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the wealth becomes a bald serpent that takes its owner by the neck and follows him until it casts him into the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: أما {سيطوقون

rows.speaker: أبو وائل
rows.claim: Abu Wa'il explains the warning as withholding relatives’ due from one’s wealth; it becomes a snake around the neck that says, “I am your wealth.”
rows.anchor: عن أبي هاشم، عن أبي وائل

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq asked Ibn Masud about the verse and was told that a bald serpent will collar the miser and bite his head.
rows.anchor: ثنا إسرائيل، عن حكيم بن جبير، عن سالم بن أبي الجعد، عن مسروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the withheld wealth will instead become a collar of fire around the misers’ necks.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: {سيطوقون

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim interprets the punishment as a collar of fire, as reported through several transmissions.
rows.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم: {سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas applies the verse to Jewish scholars who concealed Muhammad’s prophethood and urged others to conceal it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says those who concealed scripture will be compelled to produce on Judgment Day what they withheld in this life.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the serpent interpretation because of the Prophetic reports he cited, noting that no one knows God’s intended meaning better than the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأقوال بتأويل هذه الآية التأويل الذي قلناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is everlasting after all creation perishes. Calling the heavens and earth His inheritance tells people that every creature’s property passes from them at death, and only God remains to own it.
rows.anchor: فإنما قال جل ثناؤه: {ولله ميراث السموات والأرض} إعلاما بذلك منه عباده أن أملاك جميع خلقه منتقلة عنهم بموتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser’s punishment comes after death, when ownership has vanished; God knows all creatures’ deeds and repays each according to merit.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى ذكره أنه بما يعمل هؤلاء الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضل، وغيرهم من سائر خلقه، ذو خبرة وعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent before death’s throes are accepted; someone who waits until death overwhelms understanding and says “I repent now” does so without genuine repentance, like a deceiver.
rows.anchor: حتى غلب على عقله وغمرته حشرجة ميتته، فقال: وهو لا يفقه ما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s acceptance of repentance means He grants people a return to obedience and accepts their turning back from sins.
rows.anchor: يرزقهم إنابة إلى طاعته، ويتقبل منهم أوبتهم إليه، وتوبتهم التي أحدثوها من ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has always known His servants and is wise in accepting repentance and in all His governance, which contains no defect or error.
rows.anchor: حكيم في توبته على من تاب منهم من معصيته، وفي غير ذلك من تدبيره وتقديره، ولا يدخل أفعاله خلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies repentance to persistent sinners who wait until death is present, see the angels coming for their souls, and speak while death’s throes have overcome them; this is not a genuine state of repentance.
rows.anchor: فليس لهذا عند الله تبارك وتعالى توبة؛ لأنه قال ما قال في غير حال توبة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says repentance remains open until the soul is being driven out; he asks whether the verse’s “arrival” means that driving.
rows.anchor: سمع ابن عمر، يقول: «التوبة مبسوطة ما لم يسق» ثم قرأ ابن عمر

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says repentance is not accepted once death has become clear to the person.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that the person who says “I repent now” when death arrives has no repentance with God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr says repentance is accepted even shortly before death, down to an hour or a moment, and says he heard this from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، أنه قال: «من تاب قبل موته بعام تيب عليه»

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim transmits the saying that repentance remains open until the dying person is seized by the throat.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال: كان يقال

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi says the passage’s first clause concerns believers, its middle clause about sinners at death concerns hypocrites, and its final clause concerns unbelievers.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع: {إنما التوبة على الله للذين

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan says the clause about those who delay repentance until death concerns Muslims, as the verse separately names those who die unbelievers.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان، قال: بلغنا في هذه الآية: {وليست التوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse first addressed believers but was superseded by 4:48, which bars forgiveness for those dying as unbelievers while leaving monotheists to God’s will.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Sufyan’s view that the first clause concerns Muslims: hypocrites are unbelievers, so identifying them here would make the separate clause about dying unbelievers redundant; the wording distinguishes sinners from those called unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندي بالصواب ما ذكره الثوري أنه بلغه أنه في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “those who die unbelievers” is coordinated in the genitive with “those who commit sins”; they are farther from repentance because they remain in unbelief, and God has prepared painful punishment for them.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أبعدهم من التوبة كونهم على الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that people who die as unbelievers are farther from repentance.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran grammarians derive أعتدنا from العتاد, meaning “prepared”; Kufan grammarians say أعتدنا and أعددنا are synonymous, while أليما means painful.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض البصريين: معنى: {أعتدنا}

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Quraysh leaders saw Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab, and other poor Muslims with the Prophet and demanded their dismissal, promising to follow if he did so.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، قال: " مر الملأ من قريش بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also reports that Quraysh leaders passed by the Prophet and made the same request to exclude his poor companions.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: مر على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملأ من قريش، ثم ذكر نحوه

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Khabbab reports that al-Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn asked for a separate audience, embarrassed to be seen with poor believers; after the revelation the Prophet called the believers back and greeted them, then stayed with them.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الكنود، عن خباب، في قول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbab’s account repeats that the two elite men shunned the poor companions; after the revelation the Prophet called them near and sat with them until he rose.
rows.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت، بنحو حديث الحسين بن عمرو، إلا أنه قال في حديثه: فلما رأوهم حوله نفروهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Quraysh unbelievers offered to follow Muhammad if he expelled named poor Muslims whom they looked down on.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi is also cited for the report that Quraysh demanded the expulsion of poor Muslims as a condition of following Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، والكلبي، أن ناسا، من كفار قريش قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the companions as Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, whom Quraysh belittled and said they would not sit with.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa'id says six Companions, including Ibn Masud, used to arrive early, sit near the Prophet, and listen; Quraysh objected that these men were being given precedence.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، قال: قال سعيد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says prominent Quraysh approached Abu Talib, offering to follow Muhammad if he expelled their clients and allies; Umar suggested trying their request, and the verse was revealed about the poor believers, including named freedmen and allies.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عكرمة، في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that a man was ashamed to be seen with Salman and Bilal and asked Muhammad to dismiss them; the revelation warns that expelling them would make him unjust and commands that they be greeted and reassured of mercy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: قال رجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إني أستحيي من الله أن يراني مع سلمان وبلال وذويهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “calling on their Lord morning and evening” as worship through the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، قوله

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim identifies the phrase with the five obligatory prayers and argues against interpreting it as attendance at preachers’ gatherings.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حمزة، عن إبراهيم، في قوله

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim also glosses the phrase simply as prayer.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم: {ولا تطرد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means the obligatory dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan rejects the idea that the callers are story-preachers; they are people who maintain the congregational prayers.
rows.anchor: عن حمزة بن عيسى، قال: دخلت على الحسن فسألته فقلت: يا أبا سعيد، أرأيت قول الله: {واصبر نفسك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid again identifies them as those who perform the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says they worship God morning and evening by performing the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول، في قوله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the morning-and-evening callers in 18:28 as the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says the callers in 18:28 are people who attend the prescribed prayers.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر، في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibrahim identify the phrase with the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد، وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the callers are the praying believers Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib rejects using the verse to defend post-prayer storytelling: it refers to the prayer the group had just finished.
rows.anchor: فقال سعيد: " ما أسرعهم إلى هذا المجلس

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي عمرة
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Umra identifies the callers with the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عمرة، قال: «الصلاة المكتوبة»

rows.speaker: عامر
rows.claim: Amir likewise says the verse refers to prayer.
rows.anchor: عن إسرائيل، عن جابر، عن عامر، قال: «هي الصلاة»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada specifies the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid recounts that Abd al-Rahman redirected a crowd seeking storytelling to the prayer that had just ended, saying the verse concerns prayer.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: صلى عبد الرحمن في مسجد الرسول، فلما صلى قام فاستند إلى حجرة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says elites asked only that poor believers be moved behind them in the prayer rows, not expelled from the Prophet’s gathering altogether.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي الصلاة، ولكن القوم لم يسألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طرد هؤلاء الضعفاء عن مجلسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says some poor companions were with the Prophet when nobles offered to believe if the poor prayed behind them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض}

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim identifies the callers as people engaged in remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان، عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، قوله: {ولا تطرد

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim also explains the command as not excluding them from remembrance.
rows.anchor: عن منصور: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far says the callers were people whom the Prophet taught to recite the Quran.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، قوله: {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes “calling on their Lord” to mean worship, citing 40:43 where what people call upon means what they worship.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says الدعاء may include spoken remembrance, glorification, praise, required and voluntary acts; since God calls worship دعاء, the group may have combined all these, and no narrower interpretation is demonstrably superior.
rows.anchor: والدعاء لله يكون بذكره وتمجيده والثناء عليه قولا وكلاما، وقد يكون بالعمل له بالجوارح الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions sought pardon and forgiveness through righteous deeds, obligatory duties, voluntary worship, and remembrance of God morning and evening, seeking nearness to Him.
rows.anchor: يسألون عفوه ومغفرته لصالح أعمالهم وأداء ما ألزمهم من فرائضه ونوافل تطوعهم وذكرهم إياه بألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mutual-accountability clause means the Prophet is not accountable for their provision, nor they for his; fear of being judged over worldly provision must not prompt their expulsion.
rows.anchor: ما عليك من حساب ما رزقتهم من الرزق من شيء، وما عليهم من حساب ما رزقتك من الرزق من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, فتطردهم answers the preceding statement that neither party is accountable for the other, while فتكون answers the prohibition against expelling them.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {فتطردهم} [الأنعام: 52] : جواب لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الوزن is the verbal noun of وزن, with forms وزنا and وزنة; in the verse it means the just weighing on the Day people are questioned.
rows.anchor: والمرسلين، الحق. ويعني بالحق: العدل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses الوزن as judgment or adjudication and understands الحق as justice.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {والوزن يومئذ}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid separately glosses الحق as justice.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن مجاهد: {والوزن يومئذ الحق}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says that deeds themselves are weighed.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {والوزن يومئذ الحق}

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says a huge, tall, heavily eating and drinking man will weigh no more than a mosquito’s wing.
rows.anchor: قال عبيد بن عمير: «يؤتى بالرجل العظيم الطويل الأكول الشروب، فلا يزن جناح بعوضة»

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa says Gabriel oversees the scales and restores rights to the wronged; if needed, the wrongdoer bears another’s sins and returns with a mountain-like burden.
rows.anchor: عن بلال بن يحيى، عن حذيفة، قال: " صاحب الموازين يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets heavy scales as abundant good deeds.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن مجاهد: {فمن ثقلت موازينه}

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: Another view takes the scales literally as the familiar balance with a tongue and two pans, used to weigh good and bad deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: فمن ثقلت موازينه التي توزن بها حسناته وسيئاته

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says the Judgment balance is a familiar scale with two pans.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قال لي عمرو بن دينار

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says a tall, huge man is placed on the scale yet does not weigh a fly’s wing.
rows.anchor: سمعت عبيد بن عمير يقول: «يجعل الرجل العظيم الطويل في الميزان، ثم لا يقوم بجناح ذباب»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the ordinary balance interpretation: God weighs good and bad deeds, as Prophetic reports about good character being weightiest confirm.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي القول الذي ذكرناه عن عمرو بن دينار من أن ذلك: هو الميزان المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God already knows the measure of deeds and deeds are not bodies, weighing them is like recording them: it provides evidence for or against people according to their obedience, without need or fear of forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: بل ليكون ذلك حجة على خلقه، كما قال جل ثناؤه في تنزيله: {كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Amr reports that a man’s ninety-nine sin-records are outweighed by a tiny record testifying that there is no god but God and Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: " يؤتى بالرجل يوم القيامة إلى الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God weighs people by placing the person and records of good deeds in one pan, and records of bad deeds in the other; He creates the appropriate heaviness or lightness as evidence, like making limbs testify.
rows.anchor: فكذلك وزن الله أعمال خلقه بأن يوضع العبد وكتب حسناته في كفة من كفتي الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari rejects denial of the familiar balance: revelation and Prophetic reports affirm heavy and light scales, while neither reason nor transmitted proof rules this interpretation out.
rows.anchor: فما الذي أوجب لك إنكار الميزان أن يكون هو الميزان الذي وصفنا صفته الذي يتعارفه الناس؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing wrong to God’s signs means rejecting His proofs and indications instead of affirming their validity and being certain of their truth.
rows.anchor: بحجج الله وأدلته يجحدون، فلا يقرون بصحتها، ولا يوقنون بحقيقتها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses “light scales” as light good deeds.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular forms من and فأولئك are used because the sense is plural; using a singular result would also be correct and eloquent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: (فأولئك) و (من) في لفظ الواحد، لأن معناه الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse threatens polytheists who excuse indecency by ancestral custom and falsely claim God commanded it, recalling the destruction of earlier nations that rejected messengers and persisted in associating partners with God. Each nation has an appointed time for punishment, which it can neither delay nor hasten by an hour.
rows.anchor: ولكل جماعة اجتمعت على تكذيب رسل الله ورد نصائحهم، والشرك بالله مع متابعة ربهم حججه عليهم، أجل

rows.speaker: الحكم بن عتيبة
rows.claim: Al-Hakam ibn Utayba says 8:36 was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan, who spent forty awqiya of gold on the polytheists at Uhud; an awqiya then equaled forty-two mithqals.
rows.anchor: عن خطاب بن عثمان العصفري، عن الحكم بن عتيبة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Abu Sufyan brought the caravan to Mecca and summoned people to fight, leading to the Prophet’s campaign the following year; he dates Badr and Uhud.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {إن الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says polytheists including Abu Sufyan hired men to fight Muhammad; their spending would become regret and woe on Judgment Day, and they would be defeated.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " قال الله فيما كان المشركون ومنهم أبو سفيان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the spending in 8:36 with Abu Sufyan’s expenditure on unbelievers at Uhud.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {ينفقون أموالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for the account that Quraysh used caravan profits to finance revenge against Muhammad after their relatives were killed at Badr.
rows.anchor: كما ذكر عن ابن عباس أنزل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God separates unbelievers, the evil ones, from believers, the good ones, by placing the faithful in Paradise and the unbelievers in Hell.
rows.anchor: فميز جل ثناؤه بينهم بأن أسكن أهل الإيمان به وبرسوله جناته، وأنزل أهل الكفر ناره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the separation is between the people destined for felicity and those destined for misery.
rows.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the distinction as separating believer from unbeliever.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " ثم ذكر المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil are piled together, with some carried atop others, forming a heap; ركام describes a gathered, dense mass, as in the cloud image at 24:43.
rows.anchor: فيحمل الكفار بعضهم فوق بعض. {فيركمه جميعا}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the piling as gathering the evil ones together, some atop others.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {فيركمه جميعا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular khabith describes a collective, but أولئك returns to the plural spenders; they are losers because they traded wealth for punishment and earned humiliation by fighting the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {الخاسرون} [الأنفال: 37] الذين غبنت صفقتهم وخسرت تجارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three are the people deferred for God’s decision in 9:106; God later accepted their repentance. “Held back” means their repentance was deferred while others were forgiven.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء الثلاثة الذين وصفهم الله في هذه الآية بما وصفهم به فيما قبل، هم الآخرون الذين قال جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima explains that the three were held back from receiving repentance.
rows.anchor: عمن سمع عكرمة، في قوله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada likewise says the three were held back from repentance.
rows.anchor: قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة، أما قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth felt narrow despite its breadth because they grieved and regretted missing the campaign with the Messenger; their own selves felt constricted by distress.
rows.anchor: بسعتها غما وندما على تخلفهم عن الجهاد مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They became certain that no refuge from God’s trial or feared punishment existed except with God; He then granted them a return to obedience so they could comply with His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وأيقنوا بقلوبهم أن لا شيء لهم يلجئون إليه مما نزل بهم من أمر الله من البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the one who grants and enables repentance to whomever He wills, and is merciful not to punish after repentance or abandon a servant seeking to repent.
rows.anchor: هو الوهاب لعباده الإنابة إلى طاعته الموفق من أحب توفيقه منهم لما يرضيه عنه

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir identifies the three as Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn Rabi'a, all from the Ansar.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سفيان، عن جابر، في قوله: " {وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the three were deferred in the middle of Surat Bara'a.
rows.anchor: عن إسرائيل، عن جابر، عن عكرمة، وعامر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the three deferred in the middle of Bara'a were Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara ibn Rabi'a, and Ka'b ibn Malik.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also identifies them as the deferred group and names all three as Ansar.
rows.anchor: ثنا أبي، عن أبيه، عن ليث، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa'id names Ka'b ibn Malik, the poet, Murara ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayya as the three, all Ansar.
rows.anchor: عن يعقوب، عن جعفر، عن سعيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise identifies all three as Ansar: Hilal, Murara, and Ka'b.
rows.anchor: عن جويبر، عن الضحاك، قال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada names Ka'b, Hilal, and Murara as the three who missed the Tabuk expedition; he recounts their remorse and different acts while awaiting the Prophet’s response.
rows.anchor: قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة، قوله
